second_order: calling for a Warframe mark before there is a workable plan
theme_note: These codes make an initial canvas call, ask what it means, or ask whether a Warframe mark exists; what varies is whether the thin call meets confusion, anticipated deletion, a competing sign, or no answer.

second_order: catching and repairing April Fools image and wiki tricks
theme_note: Participants identify doctored or misleading visual jokes, explain the wiki takeover, undo disruptive styling, expose Photoshop, or offer restitution; the repair ranges from explanation to a technical fix or compensation.
regrouped_from: split from an initial broad April Fools grouping because catching harm and repairing it is a different practice from staging the room as another game

second_order: explaining, contesting, and closing the subreddit theme swap
theme_note: Participants identify the swapped presentation, ask for extensions or opt-outs, praise or reject it, explain its organization and value, and finally negotiate the cutoff; positions vary from delight to refusal without implying a community-wide change of mind.
regrouped_from: split from an initial wrong-game-play grouping because discussing the prank's meaning, rules, and endpoint is not the same practice as performing in character

second_order: playing the subreddit as Destiny, Club Penguin, and other games
theme_note: Members sustain the temporary wrong-game room by asking its questions, using its classes and worlds, redirecting Warframe talk, and combining game identities; performances range from straight-faced role-play to explicit collisions.

second_order: sending NorseFenrir birthday wishes across subreddits
theme_note: Members recruit greetings, supply the running joke's context, follow it into other subreddits, and receive the moderator's recognition; the practice ranges from direct wishes to explaining and tracing the flood.

second_order: using votes to make joke themes and promises happen
theme_note: Members attach joke outcomes to vote thresholds, demand delivery after the threshold, confirm the delivered Club Penguin banner, or push a remix toward the top; the promised outcomes differ but voting is the means of enforcement.

second_order: building, relocating, and defending Warframe marks together
theme_note: Participants turn canvas calls into border work, pixel placement, encouragement, relocation after loss, restoration, attack tracking, and repeated checks; the marks vary from a birthday message to the Lotus and the work ranges from making to defending.

second_order: passing joke characters, skins, products, and leaks off as Warframe
theme_note: Posts relabel other characters and images as Warframes, skins, sequels, products, or leaks, while replies sometimes extend or expose the bit; what varies is the invented object and how quickly it is recognized or removed.
regrouped_from: split from an initial wrong-game-play grouping because manufacturing fake Warframe objects and reveals is distinct from inhabiting the subreddit as another game

theme_note: A small call declares a themed day, asks for pictures of Warframes Simarising Maroo, and receives an Ivara answer; it belongs with no other exchange closely enough to merge.

second_order: comparing Warframe and Destiny for prospective players
theme_note: Participants warn, reassure, confess attachment, and make serious or joking recruitment pitches when Destiny players consider Warframe; the comparison ranges from personal history and price jabs to mechanics and community claims.
regrouped_from: split from wrong-game role-play because these exchanges evaluate the games for an actual prospective player rather than merely sustaining the subreddit costume

second_order: negotiating canvas space and reciprocity with GreenLattice and neighbours
theme_note: Members report permission, contested boundaries and interference, constrain work to approved space, exchange maintenance help, take diplomatic roles, and ask help for neighbours; the evidence varies between direct Reddit action and attributed off-platform or neighbour conduct.
regrouped_from: split from building and defending because negotiating territorial permission and reciprocal obligations with other communities is a distinct practice from placing and repairing pixels

second_order: checking late canvas designs against palette and territorial limits
theme_note: Members propose additions, test whether designs fit available colours and scale, offer conversions or alternatives, and ask whether space is claimable; outcomes range from continued willingness to reported refusal or downsizing.

second_order: recounting and appraising the finished icon
theme_note: Members display the icon, remember its earlier loss and hours of work, report defending it through closure, and assess the cleaned result; accounts vary between celebration, labour, survival, and final-state appraisal.
Confused readers ask what the canvas is and receive explanations about shared art, timed pixels, maintenance, and Drawball; both exchanges perform orientation rather than image-building.

second_order: proposing an in-game drop prank after April Fools
theme_note: A proposal makes weapon drops deliberately cruel, replies elaborate or condemn it, and calendar checks close it down; this compact practice belongs with nothing else closely enough to merge.

second_order: writing the icon into the atlas and crediting GreenLattice
theme_note: Members draft comic and formal descriptions, revise wording, and insist that the atlas entry acknowledge the neighbour that provided space; what varies is tone and wording, while public representation and credit hold the exchange together.

second_order: inviting the logo onto a successor canvas
theme_note: One post-closure author proposes placing the logo on a linked canvas and explains it as another r/place; the two-turn proposal has no visible uptake and stands as a single-exchange theme.
